facts.claim: Party Manager manages Party; a Party can be a person, company, or group, and the application lists customer, supplier, and employee.
PartyRelationship relates From and To Party and PartyRole values using partyIdFrom, partyIdTo, roleTypeIdFrom, and roleTypeIdTo.
The service boundary defines createPerson as an OFBiz operation for Person.
createPerson accepts Person attributes and returns the Person primary key as output.
setPartyStatus takes partyId and statusId and requires the statusId change to be defined in StatusValidChange.
setPartyStatus returns the original statusId as oldStatusId so ECA conditions can check whether party status actually changed.
setPartyStatus requires PARTYMGR_UPDATE or PARTYMGR_STS_UPDATE permission and a StatusValidChange.
Party ID is the system string that uniquely identifies the Party.
setPartyStatus fails when the statusId change is not defined in StatusValidChange.
Find Party presents a result list and Party details expose the complete list of user logins.
createPerson is exposed as an OFBiz java service using PartyServices.createPerson with auth set to false.
The Party documentation says a Party can be a person, company, or group and lists customer beside supplier and employee; it does not establish customer as one exclusive Party entity type.
Catalog Manager manages Product, Catalog, and Category information; Product can be physical or digital.
ProductAssoc relates a Main Product and an Assoc Product with a productAssocTypeId and effective fromDate/thruDate.
The product service boundary defines createProduct and updateProduct operations.
createProduct takes productTypeId and internalName as required inputs and productId as optional INOUT primary key.
Product records introductionDate, releaseDate, supportDiscontinuationDate, and salesDiscontinuationDate lifecycle dates.
discontinueProductSales is a groovy service that discontinues Product sales for a required productId.
createProduct is authenticated and requires productTypeId and internalName.
Product has productId as its primary key and relates to ProductType.
The createProduct contract marks productTypeId and internalName non-optional but names no fail-property in that service block.
createProduct exposes the Product primary key as INOUT, providing the created Product identifier as observable output.
createProduct is exposed through an authenticated groovy OFBiz service invoking ProductServicesScript.groovy.
The Product entity has lifecycle date fields but no statusId field; this capture does not normalize those dates into a Product status workflow.
A sales order concerns a customer, ordered products or services, payment term and method, billing and shipping addresses, and delivery instructions.
OrderRole relates OrderHeader, Party, PartyRole, RoleType, and OrderItem using orderId, partyId, and roleTypeId.
Order entry captures Product Store and Customer Details, adds items to cart, sets shipping and payment terms, and creates the Order.
createOrderFromShoppingCart takes shoppingCart as INOUT and returns orderId as OUT.
ORDER_STATUS defines Created, Processing, Approved, Sent, Held, Completed, Rejected, and Cancelled with explicit StatusValidChange rows.
StatusValidChange transition names include Process Order, Approve Order, Hold Order, Reject Order, Cancel Order, Send Order, and Complete Order.
Approved Order guidance requires checking shipping information, billing details, and requested shipping dates before Approve Order.
Sales Order document is created with a unique reference number used for customer service and issue reporting.
callProcessOrderPayments requires shoppingCart and binds a missing value to OrderRequiredFieldMissingShoppingCart.
Current order status tells the state at a given time; Find Orders lists existing Orders for completion or modification.
changeOrderStatus is an authenticated java OFBiz service invoking setOrderStatus and returning oldStatusId and orderStatusId.
The documentation says an order can be canceled only up to the final confirmation point, while seed transitions permit ORDER_APPROVED and ORDER_SENT to change to ORDER_CANCELLED.

counterexamples: Customer is documented as managed terminology, not as an exclusive Person or PartyGroup entity type in this captured evidence.
The complete captured Product entity block contains no field named statusId.
Documentation states a cancellation cutoff at final confirmation; captured StatusValidChange data permits cancellation from ORDER_APPROVED and ORDER_SENT.
